about: What a field name may be, as one list of cases read by both sides.
A field name is written as one argv token. `spec set` used to accept
anything, so datum.day's (+) form could create `my coffee`, `cups=2` and
`-weird` — names the app then refused to log to, from the chip it had just
made or from the REPL (da-b049). The rule now lives in
parser, which is the door both the terminal and the browser go through;
`web/src/lib/fieldName.ts` mirrors it for the (+) form's inline hint.
Two hand-written test files drift the same way two implementations do, so
the cases live here and both suites read this file:
`web/tests/fieldname.test.mjs`. Add a case here, not there.
`ok` is whether the name may be declared. `suggest` is the nearest name
that may be, or null when nothing usable is left; it is checked for every
case, so a name that is already fine suggests itself.
Visible characters are written literally — the unicode cases exist to say
that `café` and `日本語` are field names, and escaping them would hide the
point. Invisible ones are written as \uXXXX, because a character the next
reader cannot see is one they cannot check.

cases.name: a colon is the slug boundary
several spaces collapse to one underscore
a zero-width space U+200B is not whitespace to datum
an equals is a data key
a leading dash is a flag
a leading comma coerces to an array
a lone comma is the entry chain
